paper_a.title: Sinkhorn Distances: Lightspeed Computation of Optimal Transportation Distances

paper_b.title: Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks

metadata.description: Cuturi's Sinkhorn paper studies entropy-regularised discrete optimal transport, with core objects the transportation polytope, KL divergence, the Sinkhorn distance, and the Sinkhorn-Knopp matrix-scaling iteration. Jacot-Gabriel-Hongler's NTK paper studies the infinite-width limit of neural networks, with core objects a parameter-to-function map, a tangent (gradient) kernel, kernel gradient descent in function space, and a Gaussian-process initialisation limit. The two papers share no theorems, no definitions, no algorithm, and no proof technique; the only superficial overlap is that both incidentally invoke the general theory of positive-/negative-definite kernels in unrelated roles. We classify the pair as NEG.

matches.explanation: The only thread connecting the two papers is the abstract notion of a positive-/negative-definite kernel. Cuturi's Proposition 2 (Independence Kernel) shows that at $\alpha=0$ with a Euclidean cost matrix, the Sinkhorn distance reduces to $r^T M c$, which is a negative-definite kernel on histograms; equivalently $e^{-t r^T M c}$ is positive-definite. Jacot et al. define positive-definiteness of a (matrix-valued) kernel relative to a data norm (DP7.4) and prove that the limiting NTK is positive-definite on the sphere when the activation is non-polynomial (PrP7.2). Both invoke the same general kernel-theoretic vocabulary, but the kernels in question are entirely different objects (an OT-derived bilinear form on probability vectors vs the gradient inner product of a wide neural network) and the surrounding mathematics is unrelated. Tagged analogous / low to record the surface link, not as evidence of real overlap.

Probability simplex $\Sigma_d$ is a basic object of the OT setup; it has no counterpart in the NTK paper, which works over $\mathbb{R}^{n_0}$ inputs and a function space $\mathcal{F}$ rather than over discrete probability vectors.
Transportation polytope $U(r,c)$ — joint distributions with prescribed marginals — is unique to the OT formulation; NTK has no analogous coupling object.
Shannon entropy / KL divergence drive the entropic-regularisation idea on the OT side; NTK's information-theoretic content is zero.
Cone of metric (cost) matrices satisfying triangle inequality is OT-specific; NTK has no cost-matrix analogue.
Entropy-constrained polytope $U_\alpha$ is the central regularised object of the Sinkhorn paper; the NTK paper has nothing of this form.
Sinkhorn distance itself; entirely paper-specific to the OT setting.
Dual (Lagrangian, entropy-regularised) Sinkhorn divergence; no NTK counterpart.

Optimal-transportation problem $\min_{P\in U(r,c)}\langle P,M\rangle$ has no shared structure with NTK's least-squares regression problem ProbP7.1: one is a constrained LP over coupling matrices, the other is squared-error minimisation over a function space.
Limit $d_{M,\alpha} \to d_M$ as $\alpha\to\infty$ is an OT-internal asymptotic; no NTK analogue.
Symmetry and triangle inequality of Sinkhorn distances; NTK has no metric/triangle-inequality theorem.
Gluing lemma for entropy-constrained joint tables; OT-specific construction with no NTK counterpart.

Sinkhorn-Knopp matrix-scaling algorithm; the NTK paper presents no algorithm of its own (training is treated as continuous-time gradient flow). The Sinkhorn iteration is a fixed-point on diagonal scalings; NTK's training dynamics is a kernelised gradient flow — different objects, different roles.
Proof of large-$\alpha$ equivalence; OT-internal, no NTK analogue.

Proof that the independence kernel is negative-definite. Although it touches the kernel positive-/negative-definiteness theme already noted in the PrP5.2 entry, the proof technique (reduction to a Euclidean Gram matrix on histograms) is unrelated to NTK's PP7.5 (Hermite expansion + Schoenberg). No proof-level alignment.
Proof of metric properties via gluing; OT-specific.
Proof of the gluing lemma using the data-processing inequality; OT-specific.
ANN realization function $F^{(L)}:\mathbb{R}^P\to\mathcal{F}$ is a neural-network construction with no Sinkhorn counterpart.
Recursive definition of pre-activations / activations with NTK-style $1/\sqrt{n_\ell}$ normalisation; specific to neural networks.

Multi-dimensional matrix-valued kernel inducing a function-space bilinear form; the only kernel object Sinkhorn defines is the Gibbs kernel $K=e^{-\lambda M}$, which is a scalar matrix used inside an iteration, not a function-space inner-product object. Different role.
Functional kernel gradient $\nabla_K C$; no Sinkhorn analogue.
Kernel gradient descent in function space; no Sinkhorn analogue.
Tangent kernel of a random linear parametrisation; warm-up to the NTK, with no Sinkhorn counterpart.
Neural tangent kernel itself — central object of the paper; no Sinkhorn analogue.
Limiting NTK in the infinite-width regime; specific to NTK.
Recursive activation-covariance kernel $\Sigma^{(L)}$ for the GP limit at initialisation; no Sinkhorn counterpart.
Least-squares functional regression cost; entirely different problem from Sinkhorn's transport LP (ProbP5.1).
Gaussian-process limit at initialisation; specific to NTK.
Convergence of the random NTK to a deterministic limit; no Sinkhorn analogue.
NTK constancy during training; specific to NTK.
A-priori weight-variation control via Gronwall; specific to NTK proofs.
Spectral solution of the kernel-gradient ODE under quadratic loss; no Sinkhorn counterpart.
Long-time MAP / kernel-ridge limit of the NTK flow; no Sinkhorn counterpart.
Inductive proof of the GP-limit proposition; NTK-specific.
Inductive proof of NTK convergence at initialisation; NTK-specific.
Gronwall-based proof of NTK constancy during training; NTK-specific.
Proof of weight-control lemma via nonlinear Gronwall; NTK-specific.

Proof of NTK positive-definiteness on the sphere via Hermite expansion + Schoenberg/Gneiting. Although Sinkhorn's PP5.2 also concludes a (negative-)definiteness statement, the techniques are completely different (Cuturi: Euclidean Gram-matrix expansion; Jacot et al.: Hermite-coefficient parity argument). Recorded under the PrP5.2 analogous match, not duplicated here.
